question: Find the passage in the 100 metres article that identifies the men's world-record performance. Report the time, athlete and country, exact date, and city and country where it was achieved, then reproduce a brief supporting quotation.
reference_answer: The current men's world record is 9.58 seconds, held by Usain Bolt of Jamaica. It was set at the 2009 World Athletics Championships final in Berlin, Germany, on 16 August 2009.

question: Compute the intersection of the full nominee lists for the 68th, 70th, and 74th Academy Awards. Return every person present at all three ceremonies, attach at least one of that person's nominated works at each ceremony, and state whether any of those people won at one or more of the three ceremonies, with the corresponding award and work.
reference_answer: Seven people qualify. Kate Winslet: Sense and Sensibility; Titanic; Iris. James Horner: Apollo 13 or Braveheart; Titanic; A Beautiful Mind. John Williams: Nixon or Sabrina; Amistad; A.I. Artificial Intelligence or Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. Andy Nelson: Braveheart; L.A. Confidential; Moulin Rouge!. Anna Behlmer: Braveheart; L.A. Confidential; Moulin Rouge!. Kevin O'Connell: Crimson Tide; Con Air; Pearl Harbor. Greg Cannom: Roommates; Titanic; A Beautiful Mind. Only James Horner won at these ceremonies: at the 70th Academy Awards he won Best Original Dramatic Score for Titanic and shared Best Original Song for My Heart Will Go On with Will Jennings.
grading_notes: PASS only if all seven qualifying people are identified—Kate Winslet, James Horner, John Williams, Andy Nelson, Anna Behlmer, Kevin O'Connell, and Greg Cannom—with at least one correct nominated work for each of the three ceremonies, and James Horner is correctly identified as the only one who won at these ceremonies, at the 70th for Titanic's original dramatic score and song. PARTIAL if one to six qualifying people are identified and every supplied person, ceremony-work association, and winner statement is correct, or if all seven are identified but some required nomination or winner detail is omitted. FAIL if any claimed person did not qualify, any ceremony-work association or winner claim is materially wrong, the response says nobody qualifies, or it materially contradicts itself; an incorrect addition takes precedence over incompleteness.

question: The Best Actor award uses one procedure to create the nominee slate and another to choose the winner. Describe both procedures, including the voting method and who is allowed to vote at each stage.
reference_answer: Nominees are determined by single transferable vote within the actors branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. The winner is selected by plurality vote among all eligible Academy voting members.
grading_notes: PASS if both stages are correct: nomination by single transferable vote within the actors branch and winner selection by plurality vote of all eligible Academy voting members. PARTIAL if one stage is fully correct and the other is omitted or incomplete, with no false process claim. FAIL if either voting method, branch, or voting population is materially wrong, or if the response describes a different Academy Awards process.
